The prior attempt failed with CHECK_UNKNOWN_WORK_LIMIT — likely because work_limits was not provided correctly (the earlier call omitted required fields? I must resubmit with correct business fields: hypotheses, fixed_conditions, metrics, work_limits, acceptance_criteria, local_question, discriminating_observations, unresolved, operation, update_id.

The operation: instructions say prediction_braking uses current actual_tension_n; local_comparison requires exact adopted parameter/value plus saved effective plan horizon of 0.01 s. The instructions say "prediction_braking compares held recorded input with an instantaneous braking box solution and requires no adoption." Given the design response rejected the blanket deferral and noted prediction_braking is authorized without adoption requirements, and the sampling question can't support local_comparison (effective_horizon not confirmed), choose prediction_braking.

update_id: 34 is the terminal update, only Solve_Succeeded, adjacent to sampled settling window. Reading evidence, update 34 is the terminal update. Choose update_id 34.

work_limits: {"wall_s": 300, "prediction_evaluations": 2} — allowed limits: wall_s <= 300; prediction_evaluations=2 or local_solves=2. For prediction_braking, use prediction_evaluations: 2.

Should I also do an evidence read? The instructions: "Inspect retained evidence as needed to choose the operation and update_id." I have 2 successful reading turns already used; evidence_turn_limit 2 and successful_read_turns 2 → allowance ended. The phase instruction says "When the read allowance ends, deliver the current phase using its remaining advertised handoff tool." So make one call: diagnosis.check_request. Actually the prompt says "Use exactly one call, or up to three independent evidence reads." The evidence allowance ended, so use the handoff tool.

Let me fill fields properly.

update_id: 34
hypotheses: at least 2 competing hypotheses.
fixed_conditions: at least 1.
metrics: list.
work_limits: {"wall_s": 300.0, "prediction_evaluations": 2}
acceptance_criteria: at least 1.
local_question: string.

Hypotheses should be about what prediction_braking can separate — but must be hypotheses the probe can discriminate; if they predict the same result, say so.

Content design: at update 34, compare held recorded tension (actual_tension_n at update 34 = [3.1759, 2.7574, 1.42e-08, 0.8930, 0.1273, -0.0]) against instantaneous braking-box input over 0.01 s horizon from the saved projected state at update 34. Hypotheses:

H1 (recorded-input tangent continues to carry speed): at the saved projected state of update 34, the recorded applied tension produces an endpoint tip speed that remains above the settling speed limit, i.e., the residual motion is locally consistent with the applied input direction not opposing motion — measurable as endpoint speed difference.

H2 (braking-box input would reduce endpoint speed): instantaneous braking-box input (max opposing / decay input) would reduce endpoint speed/position over 0.01 s.

Careful: prediction_braking "compares recorded input with instantaneous braking-box input over the fixed short horizon. Can measure local endpoint speed/position differences."

Hypotheses that the check can discriminate: whether the recorded held input and the braking-box input predict different local endpoint speeds/positions, versus they predict essentially the same endpoint (in which case objective weighting vs seed selection vs backend model mismatch are not separable).

Given it's a 10 ms probe, unresolved items: cannot explain whole settling failure; objective_weighting, seed_or_iteration_plan_selection, horizon_or_deadline_effects, backend_model_mismatch remain indistinguishable; also no dominance claim.

Work limits: wall_s ≤ 300, prediction_evaluations = 2.

Let me write it.

local_question: "At the saved projected GVS state recorded for update 34 (the terminal update, the only Solve_Succeeded of 35, adjacent to the sampled settling window), over the fixed 0.01 s implicit-Euler horizon with 0.002 s step, does the recorded applied tension (actual_tension_n) and an instantaneous braking-box input predict different local endpoint tip speed/position, or the same endpoint?"

discriminating_observations: endpoint tip speed difference (m/s), endpoint tip position difference (m) between the two 0.01 s local rollouts at the same saved state.

acceptance_criteria: e.g., "Report endpoint speed and position for both rollouts with the host-bound saved state and recorded input; classify the comparison as separating the two inputs if the endpoint speed magnitude difference exceeds the settling speed scale used for the recorded window (tip_speed_scale_m_s 0.02) ... " Hmm acceptance criteria should be observable criteria. Maybe: "The check reports both local endpoint tip speeds (m/s) and positions (m) at horizon_s 0.01; the result is reported as separating the inputs if the absolute endpoint speed difference exceeds 0.02 m/s (tip_speed_scale_m_s) or endpoint position difference exceeds 0.01 m (position_limit_m); otherwise reported as 'inputs predict the same local endpoint' and no dominance inferred."

fixed_conditions: ["bound execution 5991de53e82747439e87ba8569667e1b, configuration 79466ac2..., controller 8f837eb4..., model model.gvs@1.0.0", "integration implicit_euler, integration_step_s 0.002, horizon_s 0.01", "saved projected state at update 34 from artifact b59be99... via /34/measured_initial_state; held input /34/actual_tension_n; no adoption of any weight or parameter value", "max_checks 1; backend_solves authority 0; no production configuration change"].

metrics: ["endpoint tip speed (m/s) for recorded-input rollout", "endpoint tip speed (m/s) for braking-box rollout", "endpoint tip position (m) for both rollouts", "absolute endpoint speed difference (m/s)", "absolute endpoint position difference (m)"].

unresolved: ["objective_weighting, seed_or_iteration_plan_selection, horizon_or_deadline_effects and backend_model_mismatch cannot be separated by this probe; if the two inputs predict the same local endpoint, this check cannot separate them at all — explicitly stated.", "A 0.01 s projected-model probe cannot explain the settling failure measured over window_s 0.05 inside a 0.35 s record; no dominant-cause claim.", "Per-update series (one_step_prediction, measured_initial_state, actual_tension_n, optimization_selected_iteration, optimization_raw_status) beyond update 34 were not read within the two-turn evidence limit; full warm plans and optimizer iteration traces not retained.", "local_comparison not attempted: per-update effective_horizon not read, so no saved effective horizon confirmed equal to 0.01 s."]

hypotheses (list): 
"H1 — input-direction separation: at update 34's saved projected state, the held recorded tension and an instantaneous braking-box input predict distinguishable local endpoints over 0.01 s (endpoint speed/position differ beyond the 0.02 m/s / 0.01 m scales), i.e., the local applied input materially affects the short-horizon endpoint."
"H2 — input-insensitive local endpoint: the two inputs predict effectively the same local endpoint over 0.01 s (differences within those scales), because the short horizon/state dominates the endpoint or because the braking box is not meaningfully distinguishable here."

Hmm, but the check's discriminating hypothesis should relate to candidates. Maybe a better framing: H1 the recorded held input locally admits residual motion (endpoint speed remains above 0.02 m/s), H2 the braking box reduces endpoint speed. Actually prediction_braking built to compare inputs.

I'll frame two competing hypotheses:
H1: The terminal residual motion is locally input-limited — the held recorded tension at the saved projected state of update 34 produces an endpoint whose speed differs materially from the braking-box rollout (difference > 0.02 m/s), so a local input change is observable at the 10 ms scale.
H2: The terminal residual motion is locally input-insensitive — the two rollouts agree within 0.02 m/s / 0.01 m because the short horizon and saved state dominate, so objective weighting, seed/iteration selection, horizon/deadline effects and backend-model mismatch all predict the same local result and this check cannot separate them.

Good — that explicitly handles "if hypotheses predict the same result, say so".

changed_factor / changed_value / changed_parameter: not needed for prediction_braking (requires no adoption). Leave null. But the schema allows null defaults. Also prior_result null. additional_need: maybe null. I could leave them out.

work_limits: {"wall_s": 300.0, "prediction_evaluations": 2}.

Note the previous failure was CHECK_UNKNOWN_WORK_LIMIT — probably because work_limits contained an unknown key or was missing. So provide exactly wall_s and prediction_evaluations.

Make one call.
